newsitem.title: USA: Texas regulator assails anti-oil bias of textbooks.
newsitem.headline: Texas regulator assails anti-oil bias of textbooks.

text.p: The top energy regulator of the state of Texas on Tuesday said school textbooks were biased against the oil and natural gas industries and failed to teach students about the region's energy heritage.

"What we found is that energy issues are most often minimized in content, presented with a negative bias, and what little information is provided is imbalanced," said Carole Keeton Rylander, chairman of the Texas Railroad Commission.
Rylander said a high school environmental science textbook was found to be the most biased in a study of textbooks used in schools nationwide.

"Wherever exploration for fossil fuels takes place, the risk of environmental damage is great," read a passage in the book "Environmental Science: Ecology and Human Impact" published by Addison-Wesley.

In Texas, the state's $52 billion oil and natural gas industry accounts for one in every nine dollars generated by the state's economy. But a recent poll of Texas teenagers revealed only 38 percent knew gasoline is refined from crude oil.
"Energy is integral to our history, culture, economy and future...our children are not learning about these important issues," Rylander said.
